What's inside

Five files, from plan to go-live

  • DOCX

    Performance Test Plan

    13 sections: scope, NFRs with percentiles, workload model, test types, environment gaps, test data, monitoring, entry and exit criteria, risks, schedule, roles and sign-off.

  • DOCX

    Performance Test Report

    Verdict first (PASS, PASS WITH RISKS or FAIL), key numbers, results against NFRs, resource use at peak, bottlenecks, defects, capacity statement and sign-off.

  • XLSX

    Go-live Readiness Checklist

    36 checks across performance, capacity, resilience, observability, operations, release, security and business. Status drop-downs and a summary that shows READY, IN PROGRESS or NOT READY.

  • XLSX

    Risk Register and Sign-off

    Likelihood × impact scoring with High, Medium and Low ratings. The sign-off sheet counts open risks and shows the release as blocked while a High risk is still open.

  • XLSX

    Workload Model Calculator

    Peak-hour volumes in; requests per second, virtual users (Little's Law), pacing and k6 arrival-rate settings out. Works with any load tool.

Plus a 2-page Getting Started PDF. Yellow cells are yours to fill in; grey cells calculate themselves; each spreadsheet has a How to use tab.

Free sample: the calculator's example

From peak-hour traffic to virtual users

The calculator ships with this example: production peak hour × 1.5 growth × 30% headroom. Replace the yellow columns with your own numbers and the rest updates.

JourneyPeak hour (prod)Response + think (s)Target per hourIterations / sVirtual usersPacing (s)
Login18,0001.2 + 335,1009.75414.2
Search54,0000.9 + 5105,30029.251735.9
View product36,0000.6 + 670,20019.501296.6
Add to cart9,0000.5 + 417,5504.88224.5
Checkout3,6003 + 87,0201.952211.3
Total120,600235,17065.33387

Virtual users = iterations per second × (response time + think time), rounded up. Want to try your own numbers now? The free virtual users calculator does one journey at a time.

Questions

Common questions

Which apps do they open in?

Microsoft Word and Excel, Google Docs and Sheets (upload them to Drive), LibreOffice and Apple Pages and Numbers. The spreadsheets use standard formulas only, with no macros.

Can I add my company logo?

Yes. Everything is editable: add your logo to the header, change the colours, delete sections and add your own.

Are they tied to one load testing tool?

No. They work for k6, JMeter, LoadRunner, Gatling or any other tool. The calculator also gives k6 arrival-rate settings, because they're handy.

Can I use them for clients?

Yes, for any number of your own projects or clients. Please don't resell or share the template files themselves.
